family.triumph-adler-dario.description: Compact Triumph-Adler desktops from the Olivetti era. The Dario 286 and Dario 386SX share their boards with the Olivetti PCS 286 and PCS 386SX.
family.triumph-adler-dario.history:
Dario was the name of Triumph-Adler's desktop PCs in the late 1980s and early 1990s, when the German company already belonged to Olivetti, which had bought a majority of its shares from Volkswagen in 1986.

The best documented model is the TA Dario 286, also identified as P35. Its installation and user manual, dated October 1989, describes a compact desktop measuring 360 × 99 × 312 mm, with built-in floppy drives, an optional hard disk, three expansion slots and a 102-key keyboard. Its board is the same as the Olivetti PCS 286's: Triumph-Adler's technical documentation of June 1990 matches it in chipset, memory, jumpers and Setup. The Dario 386SX, or P45, carried the same idea to a 16 MHz 80386SX; the code of its BIOS 1.14 is identical to that of the Olivetti PCS 386SX.

Who designed these boards is not documented. They may have been a Triumph-Adler design adopted by Olivetti, an Olivetti commission, or one product sold under two brands. A secondary source presents the Dario 286 as Triumph-Adler's own machine, but gives no evidence.

Triumph-Adler also used these computers as the basis of its BSS 300 and BSS 300SX writing systems, which ran MS-DOS and a proprietary word processor. According to the same secondary source, other desktops sold under the brand, such as the P92 and P100, were relabelled Olivetti M386-25 and M380 XP9 machines. In 1994 Olivetti sold Triumph-Adler to a consortium of shareholders.
